    14012018 The link layer is formed by physical hardware such as wires, or radio frequency waves. Ethernet is a standard technology, while Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and USB are popular examples of physical protocols.

1. Application
   Layer
    The application layer handles the exchange of data between applications. HTTP is a common application protocol you have probably encountered in your everyday web surfing on the Internet. Email clients use POP or IMAP to retrieve email from a remote server over TCP; and SMTP is used for sending mail over UDP.

1. Session
   Layer
    The session layer offers services which allow the hosts on one network to seamlessly connect to hostss on another network in the world. It also provides authentication, encryption, and access control.

    For instance, Network Address Translation (NAT) or port forwarding makes a complex Internet accessible via one IP address over its limited number of ports.

1. Transport
   Layer
    The transport layer takes care of end-to-end message transfer between applications on different computers across networks. Examples include Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) and User Datagram Protocol (UDP). Both TCP and UDP carry their own payload between applications
